| [N8N001](#n8n001-hardcoded-secret) | `hardcoded-secret` | high | Hard-coded secret in workflow JSON |

| [N8N009](#n8n009-pindata-pii) | `pindata-pii` | medium | Pinned test data contains real-looking personal data or secrets |
| [N8N010](#n8n010-dead-nodes) | `dead-nodes` | low | Disabled or unreachable nodes |

Severity can be raised or lowered per finding by context (for example, a write reachable from an unauthenticated trigger is one level worse). Override a rule in `.n8nlintrc.json`: `{ "rules": { "N8N010": "off", "N8N002": "low" } }`.

Suppress a single finding by putting `n8n-lint-disable N8N005` in the node's **Notes** field (with a reason). Suppress rules for a whole workflow with a sticky note containing `n8n-lint-disable-workflow` (all rules) or `n8n-lint-disable-workflow N8N003, N8N002`.

## N8N001 hardcoded-secret

**Default severity:** high  
**Hard-coded secret in workflow JSON**

API keys, tokens, passwords or private keys are stored as literal values in node parameters or code.

**Why it matters.** Workflow JSON gets exported, committed, pasted into forum posts and shared as templates. Anything literal in it is leaked the moment the file leaves your instance. n8n has a credential store and $env / $vars for exactly this.

**How to fix.** Move the value into an n8n credential (or an environment variable) and reference it with {{ $env.NAME }} / the credential selector. Then rotate the leaked value.

<details><summary>Example: before / after</summary>

Before:

```json
{
  "name": "Call API",
  "type": "n8n-nodes-base.httpRequest",
  "parameters": {
    "headerParameters": {
      "parameters": [
        {
          "name": "Authorization",
          "value": "Bearer 9f8a7b6c5d4e3f2a1b0c"
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

After:

```json
{
  "name": "Call API",
  "type": "n8n-nodes-base.httpRequest",
  "parameters": {
    "authentication": "genericCredentialType",
    "genericAuthType": "httpHeaderAuth"
  },
  "credentials": {
    "httpHeaderAuth": {
      "id": "12",
      "name": "My API"
    }
  }
}
```

</details>

## N8N002 missing-error-handling

**Default severity:** medium  
**Failures are silent or not retried**

No error workflow is configured, and external calls (HTTP / LLM) have no retry or error branch.

**Why it matters.** LLM and HTTP calls fail all the time (rate limits, timeouts, 5xx). Without an error workflow nobody is told when an automation stops; without retryOnFail a single blip drops the item.

**How to fix.** Set Workflow Settings → Error Workflow to a workflow that starts with an Error Trigger and alerts you. On HTTP / LLM nodes enable Retry On Fail, or set On Error → Continue (error output) and handle it.

<details><summary>Example: before / after</summary>

Before:

```json
{
  "nodes": [
    {
      "name": "Ask LLM",
      "type": "n8n-nodes-base.httpRequest",
      "parameters": {
        "url": "https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions",
        "method": "POST"
      }
    }
  ],
  "settings": {}
}
```

After:

```json
{
  "nodes": [
    {
      "name": "Ask LLM",
      "retryOnFail": true,
      "maxTries": 3,
      "type": "n8n-nodes-base.httpRequest",
      "parameters": {
        "url": "https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions",
        "method": "POST"
      }
    }
  ],
  "settings": {
    "errorWorkflow": "AbC123",
    "executionTimeout": 300
  }
}
```

</details>

## N8N003 unauthenticated-webhook

**Default severity:** high  
**Public webhook without authentication**

A Webhook trigger (or public chat trigger) accepts requests from anyone who finds the URL.

**Why it matters.** Production webhook URLs are guessable, leak through logs and referrers, and are scanned for. An open webhook that feeds an LLM or writes to a CRM is a free remote-control channel.

**How to fix.** Set Authentication to Header Auth / Basic Auth / JWT on the Webhook node, or verify a signature (e.g. HMAC) in the first node. For chat triggers, turn off "Make Chat Publicly Available" or add authentication.

<details><summary>Example: before / after</summary>

Before:

```json
{
  "name": "Webhook",
  "type": "n8n-nodes-base.webhook",
  "parameters": {
    "path": "lead",
    "httpMethod": "POST"
  }
}
```

After:

```json
{
  "name": "Webhook",
  "type": "n8n-nodes-base.webhook",
  "parameters": {
    "path": "lead",
    "httpMethod": "POST",
    "authentication": "headerAuth"
  },
  "credentials": {
    "httpHeaderAuth": {
      "id": "7",
      "name": "Webhook secret"
    }
  }
}
```

</details>

## N8N004 unbounded-loop

**Default severity:** medium  
**Cycle in the flow without a bound (or an agent with a huge iteration cap)**

Nodes are wired in a loop that does not go through Loop Over Items, or an AI Agent has a very high maxIterations.

**Why it matters.** A cycle that calls an LLM, an HTTP API or a write node will keep spending money / sending messages until something external stops it. Loop Over Items (SplitInBatches) is bounded by its input; a hand-wired back-edge is bounded by nothing.

**How to fix.** Use Loop Over Items for iteration. If you need a retry loop, carry an attempt counter and add an IF that exits after N tries. Keep Agent maxIterations small (default 10).

<details><summary>Example: before / after</summary>

Before:

```json
{
  "connections": {
    "Ask LLM": {
      "main": [
        [
          {
            "node": "Check",
            "type": "main",
            "index": 0
          }
        ]
      ]
    },
    "Check": {
      "main": [
        [
          {
            "node": "Ask LLM",
            "type": "main",
            "index": 0
          }
        ]
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

After:

```json
{
  "note": "Check → IF (attempt < 3) → Ask LLM, else → Give up"
}
```

</details>

## N8N005 ungated-write-after-llm

**Default severity:** high  
**Model output can trigger a write with no human approval**

A node that sends, creates, updates or deletes something is reachable from an LLM / agent node without passing a human-approval step.

**Why it matters.** LLM output is untrusted text. Anything the model can be talked into (or hallucinates) becomes an email, a CRM record, a payment or a DB write. If the workflow is also triggered by external input, this is a prompt-injection-to-action path.

**How to fix.** Put an approval gate between the model and the write: a Wait node (Resume: On Webhook Call / On Form Submitted), or a "Send and Wait for Response" action on Slack / Telegram / Gmail. Validate the model output (Code / IF / structured output parser) before it.

<details><summary>Example: before / after</summary>

Before:

```json
{
  "connections": {
    "Triage Agent": {
      "main": [
        [
          {
            "node": "Send Email",
            "type": "main",
            "index": 0
          }
        ]
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

After:

```json
{
  "connections": {
    "Triage Agent": {
      "main": [
        [
          {
            "node": "Validate",
            "type": "main",
            "index": 0
          }
        ]
      ]
    },
    "Validate": {
      "main": [
        [
          {
            "node": "Wait for Approval",
            "type": "main",
            "index": 0
          }
        ]
      ]
    },
    "Wait for Approval": {
      "main": [
        [
          {
            "node": "Send Email",
            "type": "main",
            "index": 0
          }
        ]
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

</details>

## N8N006 agent-write-tool

**Default severity:** high  
**AI Agent can call a tool that changes the outside world**

A tool connected to an AI Agent sends, creates, updates or deletes data, so the model decides when and with which arguments it runs.

**Why it matters.** Tool calls are made by the model, not by your flow. "Ask for confirmation first" written in a prompt is a request, not a control: a prompt-injected or confused model can simply skip it. $fromAI() parameters hand the model the arguments too.

**How to fix.** Give the agent read-only tools and let it *propose* actions as structured output, then execute them after an approval gate in the main flow. If a write tool must stay, use an n8n human-review / Send-and-Wait step for it, scope its credentials narrowly and log every call.

<details><summary>Example: before / after</summary>

Before:

```json
{
  "name": "Send Email Tool",
  "type": "n8n-nodes-base.gmailTool",
  "parameters": {
    "operation": "send",
    "sendTo": "={{ $fromAI('to') }}"
  }
}
```

After:

```json
{
  "note": "Agent returns { action, args } → Validate → Wait for Approval → Gmail: send"
}
```

</details>

## N8N007 sql-interpolation

**Default severity:** high  
**SQL built with {{ expressions }} instead of parameters**

A database node runs a query that interpolates values with {{ }} and has no query parameters configured.

**Why it matters.** Interpolated values become part of the SQL text. If any of them comes from a webhook, a message or an LLM, that is SQL injection.

**How to fix.** Use positional parameters ($1, $2, …) and fill them via the node option "Query Parameters" (queryReplacement), or use the node's built-in Insert / Update operations.

<details><summary>Example: before / after</summary>

Before:

```json
{
  "type": "n8n-nodes-base.postgres",
  "parameters": {
    "operation": "executeQuery",
    "query": "=SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = '{{ $json.email }}'"
  }
}
```

After:

```json
{
  "type": "n8n-nodes-base.postgres",
  "parameters": {
    "operation": "executeQuery",
    "query": "SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = $1",
    "options": {
      "queryReplacement": "={{ $json.email }}"
    }
  }
}
```

</details>

## N8N008 insecure-transport

**Default severity:** medium  
**Plain HTTP or disabled TLS verification**

An HTTP Request node calls http:// (not localhost) or turns on "Ignore SSL Issues".

**Why it matters.** Anything sent over plain HTTP (including API keys in headers) can be read and modified on the path. Ignoring certificate errors removes the protection HTTPS was supposed to give.

**How to fix.** Use https://. Remove "Ignore SSL Issues" and fix the certificate (or pin a CA) instead.

<details><summary>Example: before / after</summary>

Before:

```json
{
  "type": "n8n-nodes-base.httpRequest",
  "parameters": {
    "url": "http://api.example.org/v1/items",
    "options": {
      "allowUnauthorizedCerts": true
    }
  }
}
```

After:

```json
{
  "type": "n8n-nodes-base.httpRequest",
  "parameters": {
    "url": "https://api.example.org/v1/items"
  }
}
```

</details>

## N8N009 pindata-pii

**Default severity:** medium  
**Pinned test data contains real-looking personal data or secrets**

The exported workflow carries pinData with email addresses, phone numbers or tokens that do not look like placeholders.

**Why it matters.** Pinned data is saved inside the workflow JSON. People pin a real execution to test with, then export or commit the workflow and ship real customers' data with it.

**How to fix.** Unpin data before exporting (or replace it with fake data such as user@example.com). Consider a pre-commit hook that runs n8n-lint.

<details><summary>Example: before / after</summary>

Before:

```json
{
  "pinData": {
    "Webhook": [
      {
        "json": {
          "email": "maria.ivanova@gmail.com",
          "phone": "+7 916 123 45 67"
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

After:

```json
{
  "pinData": {
    "Webhook": [
      {
        "json": {
          "email": "user@example.com"
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

</details>

## N8N010 dead-nodes

**Default severity:** low  
**Disabled or unreachable nodes**

Nodes are disabled, or cannot be reached from any trigger, so they never run.

**Why it matters.** Dead nodes hide what the workflow really does, keep stale credentials and logic around, and are often half-finished experiments with side effects that someone later re-enables.

**How to fix.** Delete nodes you do not need. Keep experiments in a separate workflow.

<details><summary>Example: before / after</summary>

Before:

```json
{
  "name": "Old Slack alert",
  "type": "n8n-nodes-base.slack",
  "disabled": true
}
```

After:

```json
(delete the node)
```

</details>

## N8N011 shell-execution

**Default severity:** high  
**Shell command execution node**

An Execute Command or SSH node runs commands on a host.

**Why it matters.** Shell access is the highest-impact node in n8n. If any part of the command is built from input or model output, it is remote code execution on your host.

**How to fix.** Avoid it: use a dedicated node or an HTTP call to a service with a narrow API. If you must keep it, hard-code the command, pass data via files/env, and never put it downstream of an LLM or a public trigger.

<details><summary>Example: before / after</summary>

Before:

```json
{
  "type": "n8n-nodes-base.executeCommand",
  "parameters": {
    "command": "=convert {{ $json.file }} out.png"
  }
}
```

After:

```json
{
  "note": "replace with an HTTP Request to an internal conversion service"
}
```

</details>

## N8N012 code-injection-risk

**Default severity:** medium  
**Code node evaluates dynamic code or spawns processes**

A Code node uses eval(), new Function(), child_process, os.system or similar.

**Why it matters.** Evaluating strings as code turns any data that reaches it into code. Even where the n8n sandbox blocks some of it, it is a pattern that should not be in automation glue.

**How to fix.** Parse data (JSON.parse, regex, explicit field access) instead of evaluating it. Move process-spawning to a dedicated, locked-down service.

<details><summary>Example: before / after</summary>

Before:

```json
{
  "type": "n8n-nodes-base.code",
  "parameters": {
    "jsCode": "return [{ json: { out: eval($input.first().json.expr) } }];"
  }
}
```

After:

```json
{
  "type": "n8n-nodes-base.code",
  "parameters": {
    "jsCode": "const { a, b } = $input.first().json; return [{ json: { out: Number(a) + Number(b) } }];"
  }
}
```

</details>
